narrative.hero: Robust perception from optical measurements, with or without images.
narrative.bio: I study how the way light is measured shapes what a machine can infer about a scene. A single-pixel camera makes this concrete: it records one value per structured-light pattern, so any image must be computed. Three questions follow: what to measure, how to reconstruct, and whether to form an image at all. My papers take them in turn. An image is not always needed: in noise tests with clean-trained models, segmenting directly from measurements can be more robust than segmenting reconstructed images. At Politecnico di Milano, I plan to carry these questions into scattering media, using time-domain diffuse optics to recover optical properties from photon arrival times. My long-term aim is for robots to infer physical parameters and interpret their surroundings directly from raw measurements, guided by physical models.

projects.title: The Lift Spectrum · Robust image-free sensing
projects.summary: Introduces a content-adaptive 1D-to-2D lift and benchmarks it against the best clean-trained reconstruct-then-segment baselines on three simulated datasets.
bullets: Framed the measurement-to-space lift as the key design question in image-free single-pixel segmentation; designed the STSF network and the TPLS training schedule.
In simulation at 3.13% sampling: +3.2–9.9 pp foreground mIoU over SPIFS; at 20 dB SNR, +3.1–21.7 pp over the best clean-trained reconstruct-then-segment baseline, which wins without noise.
highlights: +3.1–21.7 pp foreground mIoU at 20 dB Gaussian noise, 3.13% sampling
Within 2.0–5.7 pp of its 3.13% result at 0.39% sampling
Proof of concept on a real single-pixel bench, no fine-tuning

projects.title: Sparse Hadamard single-pixel imaging
projects.summary: Tunable sparse Hadamard patterns are more resilient to noise than conventional Hadamard patterns in 20 and 30 dB SNR simulations.
bullets: Designed tunable, orthogonal sparse Hadamard patterns with two training-free modes and a noise model; more resilient to noise than conventional patterns in 20 and 30 dB SNR simulations, validated optically.
highlights: High resolution from low-order Hadamard matrices, with less memory
No prior knowledge, training or post-processing
Two operating modes; theory validated in simulation and experiment

projects.title: LDGI · Ghost imaging for optical phased-array line patterns
projects.summary: Loop differential ghost imaging corrects the spatial noise asymmetry caused by line-pattern illumination from one-dimensional optical phased arrays.
bullets: Developed loop differential ghost imaging, which corrects the noise asymmetry of line patterns from 1D optical phased arrays; orders-of-magnitude gains over traditional ghost imaging, validated with an SLM.
highlights: Orders-of-magnitude gains in reconstruction quality vs. traditional GI
A metric that quantifies the spatial symmetry of noise
Validated optically with SLM-generated line patterns

platform_copy.linkedin_about:
I am a PhD student at Xi'an Jiaotong University. I study how the way light is measured shapes what a machine can infer about a scene. A single-pixel camera makes this concrete: it records one value per structured-light pattern, so any image must be computed. Three questions follow: what to measure, how to reconstruct, and whether to form an image at all. My papers take them in turn. An image is not always needed: in noise tests with clean-trained models, segmenting directly from measurements can be more robust than segmenting reconstructed images.

On what to measure, tunable sparse Hadamard patterns make single-pixel imaging more robust to noise than conventional ones, in simulation and optical experiments (Optics Express 2025). On how to reconstruct, loop differential ghost imaging restores the spatial noise symmetry broken by line-pattern illumination from one-dimensional optical phased arrays (Optics Communications 2025). On whether to form an image, "The Lift Spectrum" (arXiv 2026, with code) shows how lifting one-dimensional measurements into a two-dimensional task representation shapes robustness.

My background spans devices and systems: I modeled electro-optic phased arrays in COMSOL and MATLAB and integrated optical systems, from mechanical design and alignment to underwater field tests. I built remote-gpu-trainer, an open-source agent skill for GPU experiments (60+ GitHub stars), and completed 13 verified peer reviews for IEEE TIP, IEEE TCI, Optics Express and Optics Letters.

At Politecnico di Milano, I plan to carry these questions into scattering media, using time-domain diffuse optics to recover optical properties from photon arrival times. My long-term aim is for robots to infer physical parameters and interpret their surroundings directly from raw measurements, guided by physical models.

I am open to research collaborations and internships in computational imaging, image-free sensing and machine perception.
platform_copy.linkedin_about_zh:
我是西安交通大学博士研究生。我研究光学测量方式如何影响机器对场景的感知。单像素相机是我的主要研究平台：它以一系列结构光图案依次照明场景，每个图案只记录一个测量值，因此任何图像都必须经计算得到。由此引出三个问题：测量什么、如何重建，以及是否需要成像。我的论文依次回应这三个问题。图像并非总是必要：在噪声测试中（模型均以无噪声数据训练），直接从测量中分割场景，可以比先重建图像再分割更为鲁棒。

关于测量什么，仿真与光学实验表明，相比传统 Hadamard 图案，稀疏度可调的 Hadamard 图案能提高单像素成像的抗噪性（Optics Express 2025）。关于如何重建，循环差分鬼成像恢复了一维光学相控阵线图案照明所破坏的噪声空间对称性（Optics Communications 2025）。关于是否需要成像，“The Lift Spectrum”（arXiv 2026，附代码）表明，一维测量如何映射为二维任务表征，会影响免成像单像素分割的鲁棒性。

此外，我具备器件与系统层面的经验：曾使用 COMSOL 与 MATLAB 对电光相控阵进行建模，并参与光学系统集成，从机械设计、光路调校到水下外场试验。我开发的开源智能体技能 remote-gpu-trainer 用于 GPU 实验，在 GitHub 获得 60 余个星标。我还为 IEEE TIP、IEEE TCI、Optics Express 与 Optics Letters 完成 13 次经核验的审稿。

在米兰理工大学，我计划将研究拓展至散射介质，利用时域漫射光学，从光子到达时间分布反演介质的光学参数。我的长期目标是让机器人在物理模型指导下，直接从原始测量中推断物理参数、理解周围环境。

欢迎就计算成像、免成像感知与机器感知方向的科研合作或研究实习与我联系。
